Samir (Support): Hey team — customer reported a weird MFA session loop after they changed their primary device. They can log in on web, but when they try to re-auth on mobile it immediately redirects to re-prompt for MFA and never establishes device trust. Happening for ~15 users in ACME Corp. Customer claims this started after a scheduled maintenance window this morning.

Alice (Support): Repro steps from customer: 1) Login on desktop, complete MFA. 2) Password change. 3) Try to sign in on iPhone app -> app shows MFA prompt, user completes it, then app goes back to sign-in screen with the same MFA prompt. No error message, just endless loop. Happens on both iOS and Android.

Samir (Support): They sent logs from mobile (redacted):
```
POST /api/session/device-trust 200
Set-Cookie: session_mfa=eyJhbGciOiJI...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=1200
POST /oauth/token 400 {"error":"invalid_grant","error_description":"refresh_token is invalid or expired"}
```
They said the mobile clocks are set to network time, but customer IT does manage their MDM, might be some NTP misconfig.

Marta (Eng-Security): Hmm. Two quick thoughts: 1) If token iat/exp validation is strict and device clock is skewed > leeway, the server would reject. 2) Device-trust cookie is short-lived (Max-Age=1200 in logs) and we rotate tokens after password change. Could be combined effect where refresh token is invalidated but the app doesn't surface an auth error and keeps prompting for MFA.

OpsBot: Noted: svc:auth-prod experienced a 2min clock skew event during maintenance at 03:14 UTC. NTP drift detected -> autosync triggered. See internal alert: <https://redwood.ops/alerts/clock-drift-18765>.

Jen (SRE): Confirmed from hosts: some auth nodes had offset ~+3m for a short period. Our JWT validation library by default allows 60s leeway; with nodes skewed to +3m, tokens issued/validated during that window could be seen as "not yet valid" on downstream checks. That explains immediate invalid_grant.

Devon (Product): Does this explain the infinite MFA loop though? Why doesn't app show an explicit error? It just re-prompts.

Marta (Eng-Security): Likely flow: app exchanges MFA assertion for refresh token; server returns error (invalid_grant). App tries to fall back to start auth flow again and shows MFA prompt. If the server's 400 doesn't include UI-friendly message, the client cycles. We should get the app to show a clear error and stop the loop, but also fix server-side tolerance.

Alice (Support): Customer provided device logs with timestamps — device time matches NTP. They also tried toggling airplane mode and reinstalling app (no change). They said web login works because browser appears to do full re-auth and succeeds after a short wait.

Marta (Eng-Security): Action items I propose: 1) Increase JWT leeway on auth nodes to 5 minutes temporarily while we confirm NTP stability. 2) Add clearer error payload for invalid_grant when due to clock skew (so clients can surface a helpful message). 3) Long-term: add a diagnostic header like X-Auth-Clock-Delta on token failure to help debugging.

Jen (SRE): I'll roll the leeway config to the affected nodes now (canary first). Will monitor metrics for increased token success.

OpsBot: Deploy started: rolling to auth-prod-group-a (3/10) at 13:22 UTC.

Samir (Support): Can we also advise customer to check MDM NTP policies? They use CorpMDM v2 and had a config change this morning per their IT.

Devon (Product): Also want a UX ticket so mobile shows a message like: "Authentication failed — please ensure device clock is correct or try again in a few minutes. Contact IT if problem persists." That will reduce support noise.

Marta (Eng-Security): Filed INF-2189 for diagnostic header and improved error payload.

Alice (Support): I pushed a draft support reply to the customer: explain probable clock skew, ask them to confirm device time and MDM changes, and offer a temporary workaround (manual NTP sync or use web).

Samir (Support): Customer responded: their IT reverted the MDM time server change after our note and says mobile logins started to work ~10 minutes after revert. They still want confirmation of root cause and a plan to prevent recurrence.

Jen (SRE): Can confirm auth nodes report NTP steady after revert, clock offsets back to <10s. Token error rate returned to baseline after leeway change + NTP fix. I've rolled the leeway config back to default; we'll deploy the diagnostic header change instead so we don't permanently widen validation window.

Marta (Eng-Security): Recommend we: 1) Add server-side metric that counts token failures by reason (clock_skew vs expired vs revoked). 2) Add a short note to runbook for oncall: "if token invalid_grant spike coincides with clock drift alert, check NTP and consider temporary leeway increase".

Devon (Product): I'll own the client UX ticket. Pairing with eng to ensure the app surfaces a non-looping error.

Samir (Support): Thanks all — I'll close the customer loop and include the postmortem steps and INF-2189 link. Marking this resolved from the customer's perspective. :thumbsup:
